title: Europe Needs a Real Policy on Israel-Palestine
gist: Koopmans and Wermenbol argue Europe should adopt 'constructive conditionality' toward Israel, noting Pew has 60% of Americans viewing Israel unfavorably (including 57% of Republicans under 50 and 84% of younger Democrats), at least seven European countries restricting arms exports, Germany and Italy blocking suspension of the EU-Israel Association Agreement despite an official breach finding, and €150 million of destroyed EU-funded infrastructure versus €1.28 billion flowing to Israeli research entities.

themes.theme: The measurable collapse in U.S. support for Israel

insights.claim: Pew found in April that 60 percent of Americans hold an unfavorable view of Israel, up 7 points in one year and nearly 20 points since 2022, with 57 percent of Republicans under 50 and 84 percent of younger Democrats unfavorable.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Bipartisan generational shift means U.S. policy support for Israel has a hard expiry date — a multi-year repricing of U.S. military aid assumptions and Israeli defense-industry dependence on Washington.
insights.quote: Pew found that 60 percent of Americans have an unfavorable view of Israel, up 7 points in a single year and almost 20 points since 2022.
insights.locator: A majority of the U.S. public now holds unfavorable views

insights.claim: The U.S. opinion shift has not yet produced policy change but is reshaping the political narrative — progressive candidates challenged mainstream Democrats over Israel in recent primaries while isolationist Republicans tested the party's pro-Israel platform.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Opinion precedes policy by an election cycle or two — 2028 is the realistic horizon for a U.S. policy reset on Israel.
insights.locator: While the popular shift within the U.S.

insights.claim: J.D. Vance, widely expected to run for president in 2028, has been reemphasizing more isolationist rhetoric on Israel in recent months.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: The likely Republican frontrunner is positioning away from unconditional support — a concrete signal for post-2028 U.S. Middle East policy risk.
insights.locator: Vice President J.D. Vance, who is widely expected

insights.claim: At least seven European countries have enacted full or partial restrictions on military exports to Israel, including Germany — Israel's second-largest arms supplier after the U.S. — which announced a partial, temporary arms embargo in August 2025.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Supply-chain risk for Israeli defense programs dependent on German components — a reason Israel is accelerating export-driven self-reliance and alternative partnerships.
insights.locator: Several European nations have taken steps

insights.claim: The EU-Israel Association Agreement — Israel's preferential access to EU markets and programs, contingent on respect for human rights — was found in official breach, but Germany and Italy blocked its suspension.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: The EU's single most powerful economic lever over Israel exists and is legally triggered — suspension is a live, unanimity-gated tail risk for Israeli exporters.
insights.locator: At the level of the EU, a change also appears underway

insights.claim: Damage to EU-funded infrastructure in Palestinian territories had reportedly reached at least €150 million by 2026, while Israeli universities and entities received some €1.28 billion under an EU research program — a mismatch the authors argue should be linked.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: EU research funding to Israeli institutions is an identified, quantified pressure point — a specific channel through which conditionality would first bite.
insights.quote: By 2026, the damage to EU-funded infrastructure was reported to have reached at least 150 million euros.
insights.locator: The EU, which remains the biggest provider

insights.claim: Constructive conditionality would mean concrete measures against settler violence — prohibiting trade with settlements and blocking export of materials used to build them — plus a response to Netanyahu's decision to breach the long-stated EU and U.S. red line on E1 settlement construction near East Jerusalem.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Settlement-linked trade bans would create compliance and supply-chain screening obligations for European firms doing business in Israel.
insights.locator: Third, any policy must have teeth

insights.claim: Gaza International Airport, largely funded by Europe at an $86 million cost and opened in 1998 as an Oslo deliverable, had its control tower bombed and runway bulldozed by Israeli forces three years later — the founding symbol of Europe paying without influence.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Historical precedent that EU development capital in the region carries uncompensated destruction risk — the basis for the authors' reparations argument.
insights.quote: When it comes to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, Europe is seen as a “payer, not a player.”
insights.locator: In November 1998, Gaza International Airport opened

insights.claim: The EU was excluded from the Trump-orchestrated 2020 Abraham Accords yet still contributed funds afterward — the clearest illustration of the payer-not-player dynamic.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: European financial contribution has historically bought no agenda-setting power — the structural problem any new EU policy must solve.
insights.locator: For decades, European policy toward Israel

insights.claim: The EU's 27 member states are structurally split — Ireland leading a pro-Palestinian minority, Germany leading a larger unwavering pro-Israel group — which has confined Europe to material assistance rather than initiative.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Unanimity requirements mean EU action on Israel will continue to lag public opinion — do not extrapolate national-level moves into EU-wide policy.
insights.locator: For decades, European policy toward Israel

insights.claim: Dutch Foreign Minister Caspar Veldkamp resigned over disagreements about tougher measures on Israel, throwing the government into further disarray — Israel policy is now a government-destabilizing issue in Europe.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Israel policy has become a domestic coalition risk in European states — a new source of European political instability to monitor.
insights.locator: This changed following Israel’s scorched-earth campaign

themes.theme: Where a new settlement would come from

insights.claim: The Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution — led by Saudi Arabia, France and Norway, backed by a declaration supported by 142 states — uses reverse engineering from the desired end state and has united Germany, Ireland, China and Russia.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
entities: Global Alliance for the Implementation of the Two-State Solution
insights.so_what: A functioning multilateral channel with unusual cross-bloc membership — the most plausible institutional vehicle if U.S. policy shifts after 2028.
insights.locator: The basis for a European constructive conditionality policy

insights.claim: Comprehensive EU policy changes emerge only in major crises or during multi-year budget negotiations, so the realistic vehicle for a grand bargain on Israel policy is the 2028-2034 EU budget talks among heads of state.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete calendar anchor — the 2028-2034 MFF negotiation is when EU Israel policy is most likely to shift materially.
insights.locator: A comprehensive European policy is unlikely

insights.claim: An EU-Saudi-Egypt-Jordan-Arab League peace initiative involving some 60 states and a reluctant United States was launched on Sept. 18, 2023 — three weeks before the Hamas attack — showing Washington was following rather than leading before Oct. 7.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Regional and European actors had already built a coalition independent of Washington — that infrastructure can be reactivated quickly if conditions allow.
insights.locator: The EU started to change tack

insights.claim: The Hamas attack killed roughly 1,200 people and took hundreds of hostages; Israel's U.S.-backed military response has killed an estimated 73,000 Palestinians to date, reduced Gaza to rubble and prompted genocide accusations.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: The casualty scale is the driver behind every opinion and policy shift catalogued here — the quantitative root of the political repricing.
insights.locator: But three weeks later the situation changed

insights.claim: Europe should also push back against Israeli military expansionism beyond its borders, including illegal land seizures and population displacement in Lebanon and Syria that hamper mediation and regional stabilization.
insights.speaker: Sven Koopmans, Grace Wermenbol
insights.so_what: Extends the Israel-policy dispute beyond Gaza into Levant territorial questions — broadening the set of issues that could trigger European measures.
